seen.extent: All 64 scans of the folder viewed in this pass (scans 1-13, 16, 26 at full viewer width, the rest at 0.75 of it; scan 8 also zoomed in the viewer). Duncan's letters in French, docketed 1730 Jan 28 to 1731. Blank or nearly blank versos: 24, 28, 32, 39, 40, 52, 56, 60. Ciphertext on 4 scans, belonging to two letters: scans 1-4 (signed 'L... 20 Janvier 1730', Q: N:) and scans 5-8 (docket '1730 ... 30'). About 17 lines of cipher by eye, not measured: scan 2 two lines, scan 6 about seven, scan 7 about six, scan 8 two. The other 60 scans have no cipher strings, including all the 'Pour vous seul' letters (scans 9, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61).
seen.cipher: Actual ciphertext: unbroken runs of digits mixed with a few letter forms, set inside clear French, with cover names in clear beside them (E: E:, F: F:, A, C, D, L). Samples read at viewer zoom, single glyphs uncertain. Scan 2, last lines: 'provisionnellement 76a5ug0 463h56a2 874ed5aq u7 g0deges 24M5u56a2 4e25e05n7. Il s'y rendra'. Scan 6, lines 1-2: 'Si C n'a pas communiqué jusqu'ici a F: F: 703u567n3672 4609m2570e465m3246009754 21732r0976e4236, qu'il lui a envoié'. Scan 8: 'ce que A a dit a 67035524609732en875 he4056 907713625e4370.' Groups such as 67, 46, 4609 and 975 recur. No decipherment between the lines or in the margin on scans 2, 6, 7 or 8; the marginal text on scans 4, 6 and 8 is clear French from the writer. Earlier scans 1, 4, 20, 30, 55 were correct that they hold no digits, but they missed the four leaves that do.

1945.key_check: Key inv. 126 tested only in part, and it did not open the strings. Cover names on these leaves do match its tables (scan 1 and scan 2). 'Supplement du Chiffre' (scan 9) gives pairs 42-89 only: paired from the start, the scan 8 string gives 67 N, then 03 and 24, and the scan 6 string 46 C, then 09, all outside the table, and the strings also hold letter forms the table has no place for. The letter table on scan 5 (a x, b r, c p ...) substitutes letters, not digits. Key sheets read: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20; sheets 6, 7, 8, 14, 16, 18 were seen only as thumbnails, which look like versos. No full transcription or solver run was done, so the digit system of the strings is not established.
1945.key_in_volume: Gelders Archief 0439 inv. 126, 'Sleutels tot het geheimschrift, 1730, 1731', 20 scans online. Scan 1 'Extract uit het groot Chyffer': Rosendael E:E:, Veldwen D:D:, de Burggraaf C:C:, Torck F:F:, Chesterfield O, and others. Scan 2: more cover names and signs. Scan 3 and 15: numbered lists (30 de Hr v. Ittersum, 70 Deventer, 800 Luisius, 900 Grumbkow ...). Scan 5: letter-for-letter table. Scan 9 'Supplement du Chiffre': A 42/43 to Z 88/89. Scan 11 'No 6': another cover list. Scan 19: printed 'Table de Chiffre' with instructions.

seen.extent: All 134 scans viewed in this batch, scans 1-134 with none left out, at the same fit-page view as inv. 124 (0.75 or 0.8 of viewer width, a few at full width, scan 10 also zoomed). Viewing covered every scan for digit runs and signs; the running text was not transcribed. Scans that first showed a blank pane, a loading wheel or a blur were reloaded until sharp: 15, 18, 38, 52, 54, 57, 59, 76, 77, 84, 87, 120, 123, 134. None failed to render, including scan 38. Blank or show-through-only versos: 4, 20, 24, 28, 32, 48, 52, 59, 60, 71, 72, 80, 83, 84, 88, 92, 100, 121, 122, 123, 124, 127, 128. Slips laid over a page at 25-29, 105-109 and 130-134 were photographed lifted too, so the text under them is seen. Dutch letters 'Doorluchtigste Prins' signed H. Vere, 's Hage 23 May to 11 Sept 1731, and memoranda ('Memorie'); scans 45-47 a draft letter in French to the King, 'Projet de la lettre que Z pourroit ecrire a N'; scans 125-126, 129-130 French copies (Seville declaration, marquis de la Paz letter); scans 131-133 a draft letter in French.
seen.cipher: No digit runs and no running sign cipher on any of the 134 scans. Clear Dutch with cover names: Z and N throughout, O, E.E., F.F., D:D:, S.S., Y.Y. Isolated code numbers that stand for names or terms, one at a time in clear sentences, on scans including 10 (800, 850), 12 (750), 14 (950, 800, 900), 16 (900), 21 (900), 22 (750), 31 (960, 970, 900), 34 (970, 750), 44 (750), 57 (900, 750), 67 (750), 73, 74 and 94 (750). Single sign ⊞ on scans 11, 15, 22, 55, 66. The writer glosses two numbers himself at scan 31, in a postscript: '960 in de Memorie vermeld is de Heer Borck en 970 de Heer ...'. No interlinear or marginal decipherment.

1946.key_check: Key inv. 126 spot-tested on what appears and it fits; not applied to every occurrence. Scan 15 of the key, headed 'Chyffer' and dated 1 June 1731, and key scan 3 give 750 een Accommodement, 800 De Heer Luisius, 850 De Scheiding, 900 De Heer Grumbkow, 950 Anglois, and key scan 3 ends with 960 and 970 (Borck and a second name), matching Vere's own postscript at scan 31; scan 10 '800' and '850', scan 12 '750 met N' and scan 21 '900' read sensibly with them. Key scan 1: Zyne Hoogheit Z, De Koning van Pruissen N, Chesterfield O; scan 45 'Projet de la lettre que Z pourroit ecrire a N', about the succession of King William, agrees. Key scan 2 gives the sign ⊞ for 'Huiwelyk met Engeland'.
1946.key_in_volume: Gelders Archief 0439 inv. 126, 'Sleutels tot het geheimschrift, 1730, 1731', 20 scans online: scan 1 'Extract uit het groot Chyffer', scan 2 more names and signs, scans 3 and 15 numbered lists, scan 9 'Supplement du Chiffre' A 42/43 to Z 88/89. The number alphabet of scan 9 is not in use on any of the 134 scans of this folder.

1946.closed: Every scan of the folder viewed, 1-134 of 134, none left unread and none failing to render. They show only clear Dutch and French with cover names, isolated code numbers standing for names and terms (750, 800, 850, 900, 950, 960, 970) and the single sign ⊞. Those spot-tested are glossed by key inv. 126 (scans 1, 2, 3, 15). The inventory's 'gedeeltelijk in geheimschrift' is met by these. No digit runs like those of inv. 124 scans 2, 6, 7, 8, and no running sign cipher. The view was fit-page, looking for ciphertext; the Dutch was not transcribed word by word.
